.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r13/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md (Known false positives: one criterion covering a whole flow)
.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r13/rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests (file list only; template judge.toml criteria not compared line by line)
evidence:
NO CONTRADICTION FOUND: I compared every pair of criteria that touch the same control (Tab indent vs keyboard exit; Save focus return vs stale-save draft retention; inline handlers in cw_html_preview vs cw_dynamic_code_refused and cw_preview_isolation; static restored picture vs cw_interaction_starts_fresh_budget; Undo/Redo availability vs replace/format undo legs) and found no pair demanding incompatible products. The scripted golden results on these bytes (editor.json, runtime.json, polish.json: every listed criterion true on one app) are consistent with that, but they are scripted checks, not a configured judge run.

DUPLICATE GRADING (the Fail):

F1. Restoring the last-good picture is a pass condition in three functional criteria, so one missing behaviour removes 5.5 of 58.5 functional weight and the trigger-specific behaviours get no credit of their own. functional/judge.toml:290 cw_last_good_recovery (weight 2.0): 'The preview must return to the most recent successful picture'. functional/judge.toml:299 cw_time_limit_recovery (1.5): 'Fails if ... the last-good picture is not shown afterwards'. functional/judge.toml:308 cw_stop_cancels_pending_work (2.0): 'Fails if ... the preview does not return to the control's picture'. The public notes state Stop cancellation and last-good restore as separate promises in separate paragraphs of behaviour.md ('Keep the latest successful preview as a last-good picture...' vs 'Stop ends the current run at once. Timers, intervals and Promise callbacks still pending from a stopped run must never change the preview or the console afterwards'). qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md: 'Share their browser scenario while scoring distinct promises separately.' The authors already use the deferral pattern elsewhere (judge.toml:254 'What the app says about why the run ended is scored by other criteria, not here'; cw_newer_run_supersedes has no restore leg), so the triplication is not forced by the format.

F2. The line and column readout is asserted in three functional criteria. judge.toml:38 cw_caret_navigation_and_line_numbers (1.0) owns it: 'check that the displayed line and column readout matches the caret's text position'. judge.toml:83 cw_caret_kept_in_view (1.5) repeats it: 'the line readout must show the last line' and 'the readout must show line 1, column 1', although the typed marker and visibility already prove the caret position. judge.toml:128 cw_undo_restores_caret (1.5) repeats it: 'and the line and column readout must show that position', although the inserted character already proves the position. In both repeats the readout clause is in the body but not in the closing Fails list, while functional/prompt.md says 'A criterion is a conjunction: every step it lists must hold', so the judge has two readings.

NOTES (not counted as defects):
N1. cw_stale_save_keeps_draft (judge.toml:362) fails 'if B's Save was not refused', which cw_stale_save_refused (judge.toml:353) also grades; cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state (judge.toml:389) and cw_newer_revision_notice_keeps_draft depend on the live refresh that cw_live_library_update grades. These are positive controls that stop a dead feature earning credit, as qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md requires ('A negative needs a successful control ... Reuse an observed fact, not another row's pass flag'), and each carries an explicit 'scored elsewhere' disclaimer for the non-control part. Consequence to keep in mind for row 40: a last-write-wins app loses 3.0 and an app with no live channel loses 5.0.
N2. The constraints gate cw_shared_saved_record (save, clear storage, reload, confirm title/filename/source) is a strict subset of the first half of cw_save_reload_restart (judge.toml:344). Gate/scored overlap is by design (zero-weight hard gate), and the scored criterion adds the restart, revision and history legs.
N3. Absence of visible Undo/Redo controls fails cw_replace_all_atomic (functional 1.5, 'One Undo with the visible Undo control'), cw_undo_redo_availability and cw_focus_returns_to_code (polish). Each observes a different property of the controls (they work, they are disabled correctly, focus returns), so I do not count it as the same observable, but it is the same missing feature three times.
N4. Multi-caret (three criteria, 5.5 weight) and Replace all (two criteria) are separated by distinct observables and carry 'scored elsewhere, not here' wording; the three visual criteria are explicitly delimited from each other. No finding.

MISSING EVIDENCE: no configured judge run exists for these bytes; the hosted run in the evidence index is on an earlier candidate, so how the judge actually treats the overlapping legs is unmeasured.
counterexample: F1: an app that enforces the five-second limit with a visible reason, shows a stop reason and never lets a stopped run's timers, intervals or Promise callbacks write to the preview or console, but leaves the preview blank after any failed run (no last-good restore). It breaks one public requirement, yet fails cw_last_good_recovery (2.0), cw_time_limit_recovery (1.5) and cw_stop_cancels_pending_work (2.0) = 5.5 of 58.5 functional weight, and earns nothing for its correct Stop cancellation and time-limit enforcement. F2: an app whose editor is fully correct but whose readout is zero-based (line 0, column 0 at document start) or absent. It fails cw_caret_navigation_and_line_numbers and, read as a conjunction, also cw_caret_kept_in_view ('the readout must show line 1, column 1') and cw_undo_restores_caret = 4.0 of 58.5, even though the caret does stay in view and Undo does restore the caret. Conversely a lenient judge following only the Fails lists passes the latter two, so the same app can receive two different scores.
suggested_fix: F1: grade restore once per trigger in one place. Either make cw_last_good_recovery own restore after a throw, a Stop and a time limit, and drop the restore clause from cw_time_limit_recovery and cw_stop_cancels_pending_work with 'whether the earlier picture is restored is scored elsewhere, not here'; or keep the legs where they are and say so explicitly in cw_last_good_recovery so it covers the throw trigger only (it already does) and accept the weight concentration with a recorded reason. F2: in cw_caret_kept_in_view and cw_undo_restores_caret, use the typed marker/character as the proof of position and either delete the readout clauses or add 'the readout itself is scored elsewhere, not here'.
